requirement: R21 (page mounted over the real diagnostics client)

entry.name: mountWithDiagnostics
entry.shape: mountWithDiagnostics(container, { fetchImpl?, baseUrl?, token?, readDiagnostics? }) - same shell/routing as mountShell, but the reader defaults to createDiagnosticsClient (real fetch client). An explicit readDiagnostics still wins.
entry.differenceFromMountShell: mountShell(container) keeps the existing no-host default (readerNotConfigured): mount.test.ts and routes.test.ts mount without a host and must not perform network I/O. Only mountWithDiagnostics injects the real client.

fetchInjection: DiagnosticsMountOptions.fetchImpl is passed straight through to createDiagnosticsClient; the e2e test supplies a stub fetch and asserts the rendered DOM, never the network.

states.assertions: each state asserts the rendered [data-diagnostics-state] plus its exact visible text (records, empty/disabled copy, exact stale phrase, exact dropped phrase, 401 vs 403 labels, 'Diagnostics read failed: Failed to fetch'); ok also asserts one fetch to /api/role-model/operator/diagnostics with accept: application/json

stub.result: stub entry without client injection: 4/4 groups time out / render the not-configured error

mutations.mutation: entry returns a fabricated {state:'disabled'} body ignoring fetch
mutations.result: 7/8 fail (only the disabled state could match the fabrication)

notRealHttp: This is NOT a real HTTP test: fetch is stubbed in-process, so no socket, no host, no credential gate, no origin/CORS enforcement, no TLS and no deployment asset serving are exercised. A live server is still needed to prove the host's authorizeOperatorRequest path over a socket, same-origin serving of the app, CORS refusal when served elsewhere, timeouts, and the deployed entry actually passing the client.
